notes:
The fake backend is the only backend checked; the sim backend was not run (it needs the pinned package installed with gymnasium, numpy and matplotlib, requirements.txt:1-3). The package serves only the pre-registered SimpleGrid-4x4-v0 environment; SimpleGrid-v0 (which requires obstacle_map) and SimpleGrid-8x8-v0 are not served, and the render modes are not exposed because cap.world.render.v1 stays unbound. The fake is a pure-Python re-implementation of the clone's discrete state machine and of the 200-step TimeLimit of the registration (gym_simplegrid/__init__.py:28-33), not the upstream environment: it draws the sampled start and goal with Python's random.Random while upstream draws them from numpy's generator (simple_grid.py:68 and :167-168), it has no renderer (simple_grid.py:116-131), and it was not compared with the upstream environment. Fidelity is F0 with timestep_ms 0 because the environment has no time base. Accepted warnings from the last gate run: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge records the seed for the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for ticks, action.index and seed (twice); these are the expected Gymnasium-family warnings (PLAYBOOK.md section 8). There were no G4 warnings. No hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); its evidence is contract_checked. No catalogue_requests: only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json: the driver declares no operator-required bound. The bridge's configured seed is 21 (driver.py, placeholder configuration), so the first episode uses that seed.
